title: Follow Tigo’s passport activation steps
plain_summary: Tigo lists the United States among the countries whose travelers can activate its self-activation SIM using a passport or accepted foreign document. Use the official activation site and follow the instructions for that document type. Have your passport and phone ready, and ask an official shop for help if activation fails. Check the current package, coverage, calls, data, and validity before adding credit; passport acceptance does not make every plan or phone compatible.

title: Check the outlet and your device’s input label
plain_summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina uses European-style Type C and F plugs. Electrical references give a 230 V, 50 Hz supply, while some visitor material still describes it as 220 V. Treat it as a higher-voltage supply than a standard U.S. outlet and confirm the actual outlet at your accommodation. A plug adapter changes the fit, not the voltage. Use a 120 V-only appliance only with conversion approved by its manufacturer.

title: Bring an adapter that fits the Dutch supply
plain_summary: The Netherlands uses Type C and F plugs with a 230 V, 50 Hz supply. Most U.S. plugs need an adapter, but an adapter does not change voltage or provide grounding by itself. Check each charger or appliance’s input label. Equipment marked for 100–240 V may work with the correct grounded connection; a 120 V-only appliance needs manufacturer-approved conversion or should be left at home.
